exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, airborne zero zero five two, contact Hong Kong Departure on one two three decimal eight.
exchanges.meaning: Tower transfers Cathay 251 to Departure, announcing the airborne time and the new frequency 123.8.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: One two three decimal eight, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot reads back the new frequency, confirming the transfer.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Departure, Cathay 251, passing one thousand five hundred feet, climbing via SID to Flight Level zero nine zero.
exchanges.meaning: The mandatory initial check-in on Departure: station, callsign, passing altitude, climbing-to level, and SID.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, Hong Kong Departure, radar contact. Passing BEKOL, climb to Flight Level one six zero, cancel level restriction.
exchanges.meaning: Departure establishes radar contact, assigns a climb to FL160, and cancels the published SID level restrictions.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Climb to Flight Level one six zero, cancel level restriction, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot's readback of the climb to FL160 with the restriction cancellation.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, negative radar contact. Scope indicates four thousand two hundred feet; you reported passing two thousand five hundred feet. Check altimeter setting and confirm level.
exchanges.meaning: Departure reports no radar contact: the scope shows 4,200 ft versus the reported 2,500 ft, and asks the crew to check the altimeter setting.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Departure, Cathay 251, altimeter setting one zero one two verified, level is two thousand five hundred feet. Cycling transponder.
exchanges.meaning: The crew confirms the altimeter setting and actual level, and cycles the transponder to reset the Mode C encoder.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, radar contact, Mode C verified two thousand five hundred feet. Climb to Flight Level zero nine zero.
exchanges.meaning: Departure re-establishes radar contact with Mode C verified at 2,500 ft and clears the climb to FL090.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Climb to Flight Level zero nine zero, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot's readback of the climb to FL090.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.meaning: The command to press the transponder IDENT button so the radar tag blooms and flashes for identification.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.meaning: The instruction deleting published SID altitude ceilings so the aircraft may climb unrestricted.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, negative! Level restriction cancelled, climb unrestricted Flight Level one six zero.
exchanges.meaning: The mandatory ATC correction after the pilot read back the cancelled SID restriction at BEKOL.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, Hong Kong Departure, radar contact.
exchanges.meaning: The canonical short form of the controller's radar identification after Mode C verification.

vocabulary.definition: The controller's declaration that the aircraft's radar target is identified and Mode C altitude verified within ±200 feet of the reported passing altitude.
The transponder altitude encoder that automatically transmits the aircraft's pressure altitude (referenced to 1013.25 hPa) to ATC radar.
The ATC command to press the transponder IDENT button, sending an SPI pulse that makes the radar tag bloom and flash for 18–20 seconds to confirm identification.
An ATC instruction deleting published SID step-up altitude constraints so the aircraft may climb unrestricted to the newly assigned level.
Standard Instrument Departure — a published lateral and vertical departure route with waypoint altitude and speed restrictions.
The mandatory first call on a new radar frequency containing station, callsign, passing altitude, climbing-to level, and SID/routing.

quiz.question: [Question 1 — Air Law & Air Traffic Procedures (ICAO Doc 4444)] When a pilot is transferred from Tower to Departure Radar immediately following takeoff, what information MUST be included in the initial check-in transmission?
options: The aircraft's current fuel remaining in hours and minutes.
The aircraft's callsign, current passing altitude, and assigned cleared level or altitude.
Only the aircraft callsign and the word "Airborne".
The aircraft's indicated airspeed and heading.
quiz.explanation: Under ICAO Doc 4444 Section 8.5.1, the initial call must include identification, current passing level/altitude, and cleared level/altitude, enabling the controller's Mode C altitude verification.

quiz.question: [Question 2 — Aircraft Instruments & Avionics (Transponders)] What barometric reference does an aircraft Mode C transponder encoder use when transmitting altitude data to air traffic control?
options: The local airport altimeter setting (QNH) dialed into the cockpit altimeter.
The height above ground level (QFE) measured by the radar altimeter.
The standard pressure datum of 1013.25 hPa (29.92 inHg), regardless of the cockpit altimeter setting.
GPS geometric altitude calculated from orbital satellites.
quiz.explanation: Mode C encoders always transmit pressure altitude referenced to 1013.25 hPa; the ATC radar computer applies local QNH to convert it to corrected indicated altitude on the scope.

sections.heading: Core Learning Content — Departure Handoff & Check-In
sections.body: Per ICAO Doc 9432 and ICAO Doc 4444 (PANS-ATM): (1) Tower frequency transfer: ATC "Cathay 251, airborne zero zero five two, contact Hong Kong Departure on one two three decimal eight." → readback "One two three decimal eight, Cathay 251." (2) Mandatory initial check-in syntax: [Station Called] → [Callsign] → PASSING [Current Altitude] → CLIMBING TO [Assigned Level] → [SID / Routing], e.g. "Hong Kong Departure, Cathay 251, passing one thousand five hundred feet, climbing via SID to Flight Level zero nine zero." (3) Controller acknowledgment: "Cathay 251, Hong Kong Departure, radar contact." (UK/some ICAO states: "Identified"). (4) Radar commands: "Squawk ident" — press the transponder IDENT button to flash the target on radar; "Cancel level restriction" — published altitude ceilings on the SID no longer apply, climb unrestricted to the new level.

sections.heading: Spaced Repetition (Forgetting Curve) Review
sections.body: Day 8 & 10 recall — (1) De-icing Type I melts existing ice/snow; Type IV is a thick pseudoplastic gel preventing new ice, shearing off at 100 knots during takeoff. (2) Cold dense air contracts the pressure column so the altimeter over-reads — true altitude is lower than indicated ("Hot to Cold, Look Out Below!"). (3) Conditional line-up readback sequence: Condition → Identification → Instruction → Repeat Condition.

sections.heading: Fun Aviation Fact Of The Day
sections.body: The transponder IDENT button: pressing it broadcasts an SPI pulse for exactly 18 seconds, making the data block blossom into a bright flashing double-target on the controller's scope — which is why instructors drill "Never press IDENT unless ATC commands it", since random IDENT presses would flood busy terminal scopes with flashing blooms.
